feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant platforms, and solid scope across strategy, web, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited quantified outcomes beyond platform scale, which reduces impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in director-level leadership; this strengthens credibility and shows increasing responsibility.  
- Strong alignment between headline, summary, skills, and experience; the positioning as a digital strategy/communications leader is consistent.  
- Good use of concrete tools and scale indicators (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views), which adds substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: include measurable results such as traffic growth, engagement increases, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, or team/budget size.  
- Tighten structure and reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Minor writing/style fixes: use “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent punctuation in lists (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. versions without the serial comma); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with tighter phrasing, one or two concrete differentiators, and less overlap with the competencies and experience sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a sharper value proposition centered on digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational leadership.
- Add one contextual qualifier such as “mission-driven, advocacy, and membership organizations” to better match the experience history.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in platform modernization, editorial workflow design, and digital governance, with a strong track record of translating complex policy and technical issues into clear, audience-focused communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Stakeholder coordination” is already covered elsewhere; consider dropping it from the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills sections. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating detailed skill categories listed elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad or generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Align terminology with the strongest evidence in recent roles: Drupal/web modernization, analytics infrastructure, advocacy messaging, and multimedia/event production.
- Reduce repetition by combining overlapping items like “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform modernization & CMS administration • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy, policy & member communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeat language already used in the header and Soft Skills.
- Several items duplicate Topline Skills headings almost exactly; consider using this section as a shorter executive snapshot.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + hands-on scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the projects footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and what is new at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact and client type: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Combine overlapping duties into sharper bullets, e.g. “Built cross-functional web and communications workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet outcome-led: mention number of sites/pages, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing speed, or stakeholder adoption if available.
- Recast the AI work as a flagship achievement: “Spearheaded AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content model, and discovery UX for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search,” microsites, and anniversary/campaign storytelling duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/platform improvement also echoes the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting ownership and current strategic scope.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will read even better if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation wins, and add outcome language beyond platform scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization win and make it outcome-oriented: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel management bullet and add performance if available: newsletter open/click rates, audience growth, engagement, or campaign results.
- Combine infrastructure/governance bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s analytics and publishing infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, while establishing governance standards and cross-department workflows to improve reporting and content operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video studio/buildout overlaps with older NACo entries on video expansion; keep this version focused on leadership and organizational impact.
- “Governance/editorial systems” also appears in the headline and competencies, so avoid repeating generic phrasing here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more operational than outcome-driven. Tighten it to emphasize scope, team coordination, and channel growth that set up the later director role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show ownership and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen impact: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling, not creation.
- “digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” also echo the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating governance language too heavily.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and recent enterprise/public-sector impact rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector digital engagement
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Enterprise web and campaign strategy” if you want closer alignment to the 2022–present work.
- Keep each line noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing leadership terms with tactical phrasing like “messaging.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale by reflecting themes from recent roles: 10,000+ page ecosystems, 50+ publishers, organization-wide workflows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat almost verbatim from the header/Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with multiple NACo role bullets; keep this section broader and less repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution strengths, not duplicate every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Cut lower-signal items if space is tight; “WordPress” is less central to recent experience than Drupal-led modernization.
- If you want more impact, make one item outcome-oriented: “Drupal platform builds and CMS modernization” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the Technical section hold the full tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies; avoid identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and business impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcomes-oriented: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI & Looker Studio reporting” is stronger than listing each tool separately.
- Replace generic terms with sharper phrasing: use “Executive KPI frameworks” instead of “KPI design,” and “Executive/leadership dashboards” instead of “Leadership reporting.”
- Add optimization language tied to user behavior: “User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity), SEO and conversion/performance optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI & Looker Studio reporting • Executive KPI frameworks and dashboards • User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity) • SEO, content performance and conversion optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and less tool-by-tool.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact framing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use broader phrasing over tool-level detail.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio buildout and operations • Multi-camera/PTZ production workflows”
- Lead with strategic/operational strengths, not generic tasks; “video production and editing” is too basic for this level.
- Combine “livestreaming” and “hybrid and virtual event production” to reduce repetition and show end-to-end event capability.
- Keep PTZ, but frame it as part of “multi-camera/PTZ production workflows” so it reads as applied expertise, not a standalone tool.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; consider differentiating this section with more senior phrasing or removing one instance.
- Tool-specific creative skills already appear under Technical + IT (“Premiere Pro,” “Livestream studio workflows,” “Podcast production”).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use this line to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeat the same tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/scope instead of just names: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing.
- If GitHub Pages was only lightly used, drop it and keep the list tighter around enterprise platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus modernization context.
- Avoid repeating Drupal/WordPress in multiple places unless this version adds scope, scale, or specialization.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Rewrite as: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) only if you want a cleaner, more senior tone: HTML, CSS, JavaScript/jQuery…
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “front-end CMS implementation,” “deployment automation,” or “serverless scripting” to show application, not just tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep them in one place or vary the phrasing.
- “GitHub Actions” may overlap with “Workflow automation”; consider moving it to Automation & Workflow Systems if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Group by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Consider trimming to the strongest/recent tools most tied to your recent roles: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira/Asana, Slack, Teams.
- If space allows, add light context instead of just names: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams — used to streamline editorial planning, approvals, and cross-team communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating every tool here if those sections stay.
- Trello/Basecamp may feel dated unless they were materially important in recent work.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and undersells a clear strength shown in recent roles: enterprise email operations and member communications. It should signal scale/use case, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms” to better match the CV’s communications leadership focus.
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: “Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp” if Higher Logic was core at NACo; otherwise keep the most-used platform first.
- If accurate, add functional context instead of only names: “Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp — newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign journeys, member communications”
- Keep it concise; avoid slash-heavy phrasing. “Customer Insights / Journeys” could be simplified to the current product name you actually used.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets about email/newsletters; don’t repeat outcomes here.
- If you add “audience segmentation” or “campaign journeys,” avoid repeating similar wording under Automation & Workflow Systems.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, add 1–2 concrete outputs or scale indicators.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Replace vague phrases like “high-impact digital content” with specifics: mention volume/frequency, audience, or flagship formats if known.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update, and helped standardize day-to-day digital workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” rather than “guidance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this item as launching or early production of the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple NACo entries; here, focus on building the initial team and foundational processes.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific verb: “produced” or “developed multimedia and digital content assets.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program support first, then media innovation second, to show breadth without overexplaining.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this brief so the podcast launch remains the standout point.
- Avoid claiming broader digital leadership here, since that is better established in 2015–2024 roles.
